steps.text: Place black-eyed peas into a large container and cover with several inches of cool water; let soak at room temperature, 8 hours to overnight. Drain and rinse; set aside.

Heat olive oil in a large stockpot over medium heat. Add onion and garlic; cook and stir until onion becomes translucent, about 5 minutes. Pour in broth and water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. Stir in black-eyed peas, ham hocks, tomatoes, pepperoncini, bay leaf, garlic powder, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Cover and simmer until peas are tender, ham meat is falling off the bones, and broth is thickened, about 3 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: New Year Black-Eyed Peas
raw_recipe.description: These hearty black-eyed peas are simmered with smoked ham hocks, tomatoes, and pepperoncini peppers for a subtle kick and touch of sweetness.

video.description: According to Southern tradition, eating black-eyed peas on New Year's Day will bring a year's worth of good luck and/or monetary gain. In this video, Nicole shows you how to make new year black eyed peas for your end of the year festivities. A can of black eyed peas give you so many options as a side dish, whether you cook the peas on their own or add in a ham hock with diced tomatoes. Give your dinner plate some luck and flavor going into this new year.

review.reviewBody: 1. The pepperocinis are those (very mild) yellow peppers that you often get whole on top of Greek salads... they will not make this dish spicy, but add a very special flavor to it. I would not reccommend leaving them out. You can find them at any grocery store - they are in jar near where you find the olives. If you would like the peas to be spicy, by all means add some other peppers or even some cajun seasoning. 2. The ham hocks that are called for do not offer any meat to be eaten - they serve the purpose of flavoring the peas. If you would like chunks of meat in the peas, use another type of ham as well as the hocks (as the flavor that the bones and skin impart are the signature flavor of traditional southern black-eyed peas) 3. If you would like less liquid in the peas, or a thicker sauce, reduce the water by half and/or add a tablespoon of flour to the sauteed onion to make a sort of paste before adding the liquids.

I wish I could give this 5 stars because the flavor was very nice. That being said the instructions were way off fluid wise. When I added the 8 cups of water it seemed like too much but I didn't want to ruin the recipe figuring the chef new best. Then I read some of the reviews and realized I was not alone. Then I watched the video and lo and behold she did NOT add the 8 cups of water, only the 2 cartons of broth! I decided to discard about 5 cups of the fluid from my stockpot (which was way too full) and which resulted in nicely cooked and flavorful black-eyed peas. I would make this recipe again only omitting the extra water (or only adding ~1-2 cups if needed).

I mostly followed this recipe with a few changes. I brined the black eyed peas overnight in 4 quarts of water with 2T of kosher salt. I added another onion, 2 extra cloves of garlic, 2 stalks celery, and 2 medium carrots. I sauteed the veggies in 2T of duck fat. I used fresh thyme. For the ham, I used a frozen bone with meat on it from the the honey baked store in my town. I simmered everything (except the extra water) together except the beans for a couple of hours, then added the rinsed beans and cooked it another couple of hours. I added the peperoncini and left them in for about 30 minutes after I added the beans, and the broth was getting very spicy, so I removed them and finished cooking the stew. It still had a nice kick, but it wasn't super spicy. Everybody raved about it. It needed no extra salt. This is a great recipe.
Followed the recipe … way too much water…so it is bland! I would suggest just the chicken stock and enough water to cover…with all that liquid it does take more than 3 hours to cook !

I think the 8 cups of water are meant to presoak the peas, not add to the broth. Watch the video. She doesn't add water to the broth. I used 2 cups of water (before watching the video) and had to cook uncovered for a while to reduce the liquid. Other than that, it was great. Used the peperocini and a little brine.

I made this recipe for New Year's Day and really enjoyed the outcome. But I did not add the 8 cups of water in addition to the broth. Frankly, I don't own a pan large enough to all of that liquid plus the pound of beans and 2 ham hocks. It still provided my husband and me with 3 meals.

wonderful recipe - the peppericini made it; juts a slight amount of heat - I had a spiral sliced ham bone which provided diced ham as well as some ham off the bone - peas, onions and ham were delicious - the broth is luxurious - just make sure to not over cook the peas
I enjoyed this, but agree with those who said there’s too much water, and I used 7 instead of 8 cups. I used frozen black eyed peas, and couldn’t find any ham hocks, added some bacon and ham instead.

We LOVED this dish. I made New Year's dinner for my wife & thought I'd give this one a try (even though I never really cared for peas. I used 2 cans of black eyed peas (probably could've added another) since I saw recipe in the morning & wanted to try it that night! Also I threw in a couple slices of chopped ham from the Christmas leftovers. Ok, as many reviewers have stated- there is a lot of liquid. I used the called for amount of chicken broth & only 2 cups of water. STILL too much liquid. For us, the dish turned out spicy. I used REGULAR pepperocinis- and yes they DO create a spicy after taste in the back of your throat. Since my wife doesn't like spicy food, she (being a great cook) "rescued" my dish by extracting 2 cups of the cooked broth from the pot, adding 1-2 tbl spoons of sugar, a 6 oz can of tomato paste, and another cup of chicken broth - all to "knock down" the spicy kick. We LOVED it!! I will definitely make this again. VERY flavorful & hearty. I was sad when we ate the last of it! Perhaps I will just use one pepperocini next time ;)

Sweet stuff!! I made with just a few revisions...so good I downed the first bowl in minutes!!! Great with a sweet cornbread! I used: white onion..had no yellow....extra fresh garlic (omitted the garlic powder)..omitted the water..used all the liquid from the canned tomatoes PLUS a can of stewed tomatoes...added extra ham (big chunks)...used three small ham hocks...cause thats what came in the package =). I did not have bay leaf..and I only used salt and pepper when cooking the onions and garlic in the oil...this is so good..I just cannot believe it! // side note..I'm not sure what size pot the original recipe used...but my biggest stock pot was FULL without the addition of water...and I had plenty of "juice" .

I gave this recipe five stars even though I have not finished it yet. I used the biggest Dutch oven I have and if I had added 8 cups of water in addition to the two boxes of chicken broth my pot would not have been big enough! So I’m just going with the broth and if it boils down too much I will add some water. Smells good simmering!
It was very good and we will definitely make this again. We however didn’t have pepperoncini and we only added 4 cups of water. We added cubed ham and more garlic. Turned out perfect.

We always eat black-eye peas for New Years. This year we decided to try this recipe and change it up. It is a new family favourite!! We used the leftover Christmas ham without the bone (having used the bone for split pea soup). We had it with corn bread and swiss chard from our garden. Amazing since we live on Vancouver Island and it is January 1st.

Instead of smoked sausage I substituted grounded italian sausage. Bite size potatoes for starch (thickness and taste) Jalapeno take seeds out. Cut into small pieces add for a bit of spice. Serve with drained small canned corn to corn bread cooked mix (add corn in mix) a small dolip of sour cream and parsley diced Yummy

Great recipe! If I had read the comments first I would have omitted a quart of water; this is soupier than I anticipated but the broth is delicious sopped up with crusty bread. I added a splash of the pepperoncini brine, doubled the garlic, and threw in several handfuls of chopped curly kale at the very end. Happy new year!
It was great! I added some spicy sausage and used 2 32 oz chicken broths and 2 cups of water. I used Rotel also. It was delicious!
Delicious! Easy to prepare. Like others have said, follow the video and omit the water.
Like the recipe. Added a few items celery and carrots and use Wonder to thicken a little. Added a tbs of butter at the end. Yummy

I am so grateful for finding this recipe years ago! I make this recipe for every New Year’s Day and cannot rave enough about how good they taste!! So easy to make and absolutely the BEST recipe for New Year’s black eyed peas!
